This is the same SC-3366 large-order governor-limit failure mode (32 lines), now manifesting in the asset-creation transaction. found.rootCause: PricingTermCount on TermDefined QuoteLineItems is a platform read-only field (no formula) that only the native RLM pricing/term-derivation engine can populate during a Reprice/PlaceQuote pass. Around 2026-06-11 the pricing procedure was republished (V12->V13) and the context definition / term-derivation step that emits PricingTermCount was no longer wired correctly (same context-resync regression family as the 'Specify the contextDefinitionName' Reprice gack — pricing completes 'CompletedWithPricing' but PricingTermCount is not written). Every other standard term field (StartDate, EndDate, SubscriptionTerm, units, PricingTerm) IS still derived, so PricingTermCount became the sole null. Because there is no Fortra quote-side flow that backstops these standard term fields (only the order-side Fortra_OrderItem_Set_Dates exists, and even that wrote only custom billing fields until SC-3411 V6 added the standard EndDate/PTC backstop), the null PricingTermCount reaches the quote, is copied onto the OrderItem at convert, and RLM blocks activation of the un-termed line. This is a pricing-engine/context regression, not a data-quality or product-config defect (PSMO config is identical across working and broken products, and all inputs to derive PTC — EndDate-StartDate over a 1-Annual term = 1.0 — are present).
found.resolution: Quote-side resolution, in priority order. PRIMARY (fix the engine, the true platform-correct fix): re-sync the context definition (SalesTransactionContextExt_v2 family) to the active V13 pricing procedure and re-verify the term-derivation step/output mapping that emits PricingTermCount — this is the same resync that fixes the related V13-republish context gack. Validate by re-pricing one repro line (e.g. 0QLWC000003e38j4AA) in a sandbox and confirming PricingTermCount populates to 1.0 with no manual edit. This restores correct behavior for ALL TermDefined products at once and is the durable answer to 'what SHOULD derive it.' INTERIM/BELT-AND-SUSPENDERS (declarative, no engine dependency, mirrors the order-side SC-3411 V6 pattern at the quote): add a before-save record-triggered flow on QuoteLineItem — call it Fortra_QuoteLineItem_Set_Term_Fields — gated EXACTLY like V6 (SellingModelType=TermDefined AND PricingTermCount IsNull AND EndDate IsNotNull AND StartDate IsNotNull), that computes PricingTermCount from the dates and PricingTermUnit (Annual => years between Start and End, rounded; here = 1) and stamps the standard PricingTermCount. This is safe: QuoteLineItem.PricingTermCount is NOT directly writable via API, so the flow must set it via a formula/assignment in the before-save context where the platform allows the standard field write, OR (if blocked) set SubscriptionTerm/dates only and rely on the engine — TEST writability of PricingTermCount in a before-save QLI flow first, because the describe shows updateable=false (this is the key feasibility unknown and must be proven before committing to the declarative path; if not writable, the engine resync is the ONLY option). Self-gated so it never touches healthy lines, OneTime lines (PTC=0), or lines with already-derived PTC. Tie-in to SC-3390/Instant-Pricing-OFF: because Instant Pricing is OFF on the line editor, term fields are only (re)derived on SAVE/Reprice, so the before-save flow is the correct hook point and will run on every save. PROD-SAFETY: all of this is UAT-only investigation; the engine resync and any new quote flow are config/metadata deploys that MUST be validated in UAT against the live V13 procedure (always retrieve live, versions move daily) and require fresh explicit deploy authorization — do not deploy to prod (prod is pre-cutover and these term fields/flows are UAT-only). found.summary: SC-3415 is two independent defects. Defect #1 (no Assets on activation) is NOT globally broken (org has 430,330 lifecycle-managed assets, 125 in 7 days).
